assessment.scope: Repository implementation, delivery/runtime controls, governance evidence and AI-assisted SDLC. Missing claims are intentionally not assessed.

aggregation.notes: Consumers must preserve repository/evidence provenance and assessment coverage. Missing claims are not zero. Assessments from different DSOMM source commits must be normalized to an explicit target model before portfolio aggregation.

claims.rationale: The repository defines deterministic build commands and enforces production builds in CI.

claims.activityName: Building and testing of artifacts in virtualized environments
claims.rationale: Pull-request validation builds and tests artifacts on hosted runners and the fallback image in Docker.
Security-critical GitHub Actions and the Semgrep image are pinned immutably, while not every runtime dependency is content-addressed.
No generated CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM is currently published as a repository or release artifact.
Production and preview deployment use Vercel Git Integration with automated preview validation.
The production/preview boundary and deployment validation are explicitly documented and tested.
Runtime secrets are provided through deployment/CI secret stores and the repository forbids committed secrets.

claims.activityName: Evaluation of the trust of used components
claims.rationale: Dependency changes are reviewed and vulnerability scanning is present, but a formal trust/admission policy such as Scorecard or repository firewall is not yet enforced.
Dependency ownership, cadence, vulnerability handling and rebase policy are versioned.
Renovate configuration exists, but the roadmap records that live Renovate activation has not yet been proven.

claims.activityName: Conduction of simple threat modeling on technical level
claims.rationale: A repository-specific STRIDE model documents eight threat scenarios and mitigations. This is initial design evidence only: independent review, runtime validation and repeatable mitigations are not yet complete.
Security targets and quality/security invariants are documented in the repository and the broader DevSecOps operating model.

claims.activityName: Creation of threat modeling processes and standards
claims.rationale: A reusable threat-model approach is documented in Notion, but this repository does not yet carry its own threat model or a mandatory trigger.
Security scanning and review expectations are systematic, but live branch protection does not yet guarantee independent security review for every merge.
A Security Champions and coaching model is documented, but operating cadence and participation are not evidenced by this repository.
The broader Nabla model defines criticality tiers and risk-based controls; repository-specific classification remains incomplete.

claims.activityName: Approval by reviewing any new version
claims.rationale: PR review and exact-SHA evidence are the intended flow, but the live master ruleset that makes review mandatory is still absent.

claims.activityName: Definition of a change management process
claims.rationale: The repository defines a deterministic change state machine, CI gates and rollback-oriented rules, while formal live branch enforcement remains incomplete.
Security headers are configured and covered by application security baseline tests.
Source, configuration, policy, tests and assessment data are maintained in Git.
The repository policy and target ruleset require PR-based delivery, but the last live audit found the GitHub ruleset missing.
The versioned target ruleset blocks non-fast-forward updates, but the live repository audit records that the ruleset is not installed.
Local preventive secret checks and hosted secret scanning exist; server-side push protection enforcement is not proven by the repository contract.
The application registers OpenTelemetry in Vercel, but the repository does not yet expose a complete operational metric SLO contract.
Vercel provides centralized runtime observability and OTel instrumentation is registered, while automated log retrieval remains an open roadmap item.
GitHub security scanners and deployment security workflows produce centralized security events, but a unified runtime security-event stream is not evidenced.
CI and deployment failures surface alerts/statuses, but an explicit production alerting/SLO policy for this site is not yet versioned.

claims.activityName: Security unit tests for important components
claims.rationale: Security and policy contracts are exercised by the repository unit-test suite.

claims.activityName: Security integration tests for important components
claims.rationale: Preview security and integration browser tests run against deployed candidates.
Fallback containers and production deployments have explicit smoke validation.

claims.activityName: Treatment of defects with high or critical severity
claims.rationale: Security findings block relevant gates and vulnerability remediation policy exists, but an explicit repository SLA/exception workflow is not fully evidenced.
OWASP ZAP scans Preview and production surfaces.
The local-first quality gate and preventive hooks are explicit repository contracts.
npm audit/Snyk and dependency vulnerability handling exist, but the dedicated SCA evidence chain and SBOM are incomplete.

claims.activityName: Static analysis for important client side components
claims.rationale: Semgrep and CodeQL cover the JavaScript/TypeScript application and current exact-SHA checks are green.

claims.activityName: Static analysis for important server side components
claims.rationale: Server-side Next.js code is included in Semgrep/CodeQL and quality gates.
Semgrep, CodeQL, GitGuardian, ZAP, browser security tests and optional Snyk provide independent analyzers.

claims.activityName: Test for stored secrets in code
claims.rationale: Private-key/secret preventive checks and hosted secret scanning are active in the validation chain.
Repository agent rules are versioned and loaded as persistent project guidance.
Repository-specific agent rules and a broader AI security framework exist, but a single formal AI-use policy/inventory is not yet published in this repository.
The repository distinguishes agent/tool classes and workflows, but it does not yet publish a normalized machine-readable inventory of approved coding agents and MCP integrations.

claims.activityName: Language and framework specific security rules
claims.rationale: The repository provides Next.js/frontend/security guidance and deterministic framework-specific quality tools for agents.
Agent work follows explicit task cards, roadmaps and deterministic phases, but not every change starts from a formal specification artifact.
AI threat-model principles exist in the governing framework, but repository agent instructions do not yet mandate a threat-model trigger for security-significant changes.
Agent instructions constrain tools, branch mutation and publication, but external enforcement of every agent permission is not demonstrated by this repository.

claims.activityName: Human review of AI generated plans
claims.rationale: The workflow expects review before publication/merge, while mandatory server-side human approval is not yet proven.

claims.activityName: Human review of AI generated specifications
claims.rationale: Specifications and roadmaps are reviewable in Git/Notion, but mandatory independent approval is not technically enforced.
Agents are required to run deterministic fix/review/prove phases and exact-SHA validation before publication.

claims.activityName: Static and dynamic analysis of AI generated code
claims.rationale: Published agent changes enter the same Semgrep/CodeQL and Preview/ZAP/Playwright security gates as human changes.
Dependency changes are governed by Renovate/security policy and CI, but dedicated AI-origin dependency provenance is not separately recorded.

claims.activityName: Human review of AI generated code
claims.rationale: Human merge remains the intended control point, but branch protection does not yet prove mandatory independent review for every AI-generated change.

claims.activityName: No verification bypass for AI generated code
claims.rationale: Repository policy forbids weakening quality gates and exact-SHA proof, but the missing live ruleset means server-side bypass resistance is incomplete.
The public site does not expose an AI assistant or model-response surface; AI is used in the development process instead.

claims.activityName: Secure output handling in AI applications
claims.rationale: The public site has no runtime model output to validate or render.

claims.activityName: Protection of agent memory against poisoning
claims.rationale: The public site has no persistent runtime AI-agent memory; coding-agent workspace controls are assessed separately.
